message.content:
According to the source [Zilpo Road], Zilpo Road "can be accessed by U.S. Highway 60." 
According to the sources [Morehead, Kentucky], [Hawks Nest, West Virginia], and [Glen Ferris, West Virginia], U.S. Route 60 is also known as the Midland Trail. 

Final answer: U.S. Highway 60
message.reasoning:
The question asks: "What U.S Highway gives access to Zilpo Road, and is also known as Midland Trail?"
Looking at the sources:
[Zilpo Road] says: "The nine mile byway starts south of Morehead, Kentucky and can be accessed by U.S. Highway 60."
[Morehead, Kentucky] says: "Morehead is a home rule-class city located along US 60 (the historic Midland Trail)..."
[Hawks Nest, West Virginia] says: "In modern times, the Midland Trail carries U.S. Route 60 through the same general route."
[Glen Ferris, West Virginia] says: "The sole highway linking Glen Ferris to the area is U.S. Route 60, known also as the Midland Trail."
[Peterman Hill] says: "The road was originally known as Midland Trail and later U.S. 60 alternate until 1964..."
[California State Route 266] says: "The southern portion of the highway, along with modern SR 168, dates to the auto trail era, forming part of the Midland Trail."

So the U.S. Highway that gives access to Zilpo Road is U.S. Highway 60, which is also known as the Midland Trail.
